Kate — thanks, happy to take point. I looped in Sergio (solutions) and Karthik (performance engineering) to craft a MAP scope focused on your claims automation workload.

High level we propose:
- Workload slices: 
  1) Inference short (20-80 tokens) — chat/intent classification surface (60% of traffic)
  2) Medium (80-300 tokens) — templated claim summarization (30% of traffic)
  3) Long (300-1024 tokens) — document extraction + summarization (10% of traffic)
- QPS targets: baseline 25 qps, expected pilot peak 75 qps, stress runs to 200 qps (burst simulation).
- Concurrency: pilot target concurrency 40 active sessions, scale test to 160 concurrent sessions.
- TTFT metric: time-to-first-token measured per-request (start of server-side response to first token emitted).
- Success criteria (proposal):
  • TTFT p50 < 120ms for short; p95 < 300ms
  • TTFT p50 < 200ms for medium; p95 < 500ms
  • TTFT p50 < 300ms for long; p95 < 900ms
  • Sustained throughput at pilot QPS with <2% error rate
  • Memory/KV cache hit targets > 65% for repeated session archetypes

We will draft into a one-page MAP bench scope and share the artifact (PDF + CSV workload profile). Can you confirm whether Aegis requires encrypted KV cache or any additional telemetry redaction for test runs?

Vanessa Ortiz

Looping in Karthik and Priyom for perf details. Quick notes from the runtime side:

- Kernel/quantization plan: We'll run first with FP16 optimized variant, then a 4-bit quantized variant for cost comparison. Expect ~10-18% TTFT delta for long-form loads on 4-bit; we'll document per-model.
- Batching policy: dynamic batching with a target batching window of 8-12ms to balance latency vs throughput. We will run an explicit series with batching disabled to characterize worst-case TTFT.
- KV cache profile: we'll instrument session locality for claim threads — recommend enabling prefix caching for 7-day reuse in pilot.
- Test harness: Redwood load runner + Aegis synthetic corpus (we will need the representative sample corpus).

Proposed bench schedule (two-week pilot):
1) Week 1: baseline runs + short form TTFT profile (day 1-3), medium/long stability runs (day 4-5)
2) Week 2: stress/concurrency + fallback scenarios (day 1-3), report generation & sign-off (day 4-5)

I'll prepare a topline runbook and acceptance matrix. Vanessa: can you ask Kate for a 250–500 message sample (anonymized) to seed the workload profile?

Sergio
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

- Compliance: Redwood will run the bench in a customer-scoped Private pilot environment. For the duration of the MAP we will:

  • Apply deterministic redaction for token spans flagged as PII by the Aegis schema (we'll share the redaction mapping).
  • Strip any attachments during the run — we will accept a metadata-only manifest.
- Turnaround: yes — we commit to delivering a final bench report and a go/no-go recommendation within 48 business hours after the final test completes (report generation scheduled as part of Week 2 day 4).

Deliverables we will attach to the MAP:
- aegis_map_final_report.pdf (bench results, per-slice SLOs, model/quantization comparison)
